title: Assessment of Inflammatory and Chemical Parameters in Serum and Intraocular Samples of Patients with Various Ocular Diseases: The Homburg Inflammation Study (HIS)
summary:
Investigation of inflammatory biomarkers in common eye diseases

In this study, we want to find out whether certain inflammatory substances in the blood or eye fluid are more common in people with different eye diseases. These diseases include age-related macular degeneration, diabetic macular edema, keratoconus, and a specific type of retinal disorder called central serous chorioretinopathy.

The samples will be taken during medical procedures that are already planned, such as surgeries or eye injections. This means that participants will not have to undergo any extra tests or face additional risks.

The goal of this study is to better understand how these diseases develop and progress. The findings could help in the future to create new and improved treatment options.
conditions: The study investigates inflammatory processes in various eye diseases: keratoconus, age-related macular degeneration (AMD), diabetic macular edema (DME), central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC), as well as cataract (used as a comparison group). The aim is to identify immunological differences between these conditions. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age over 18 years
2. Written informed consent given by the participant or their legal representative
3. Presence of one of the following diagnosed eye diseases:
Kerotoconus (KK)
- Age-related macular degeneration (AMD)
- Diabetic macular edema (DME)
- Central serous chorioretinopathy (CCS)
- Cataract
Exclusion criteria:
1. Lack of consent or inability to consent without a legal guardian.
2. Pregnancy.
3. Pre-existing eye diseases diagnosed by an ophthalmologist that could cause inflammation, such as uveitis or scleritis.
4. Prior keratoplasty in keratoconus patients.
5. Previous intravitreal injection therapy (IVOM) and other retinal diseases in AMD and DME patients.
6. Other retinal diseases in CCS patients.
